title: Commbank Earn up to $420 Cashback - How Do I Avoid Fail?
body:
T&C:
The first eligible spend period will commence from the day your account is opened, up to the end of your second statement period after account opening. This means your first eligible spend period may be longer than one statement period. After this date, the offer spend requirements will align to each statement period that follows, for up to six eligible statement periods in total.
Transactions must be fully processed and posted to your account within 14 days of the transaction date to be eligible and will be allocated to the statement period in which the transaction date occurred. This means a transaction may appear on a later statement but still be counted toward the minimum spend requirement for an earlier statement period.
https://www.commbank.com.au/credit-cards/low-rate.html
Seems like easy money — just $6 per month for 6 months!
Questions:
Q1: Eligible Spend
I assume council rates, ATO payments and car registration fees are still not eligible expenses.
What about purchasing prepaid Visa or Mastercard gift cards from Coles, or using a Zip credit card and then paying off the Zip balance with a CommBank credit card?
Would both ways qualify as eligible spending?
Would both be considered eligible spending?
Q2: This means a transaction may appear on a later statement but still be counted toward the minimum spend requirement for an earlier statement period.
Does this mean we can receive two $70 cashback rewards in one statement period:
one for an eligible transaction from the previous period
and another for an eligible transaction from the current period
as long as the total allowance of 6 × $70 cashback rewards has not been exceeded?
Q3: Can I take up this offer later and earn up to $240 cashback on the CommBank Low Fee Credit Card ($3/month) after completing the Low Rate Credit Card offer above?
